messages:
From: Claire Owens <security@nimbushealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:14:22 -0800
Subject: Request: mapping of third-party responsibilities for SIG review

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for taking our SIG packet. As part of our vendor review we need a concise mapping of Redwood's third-party services and what they are authorized to do (we'll use this to populate the SIG Subprocessors section). Specifically, can you provide a table that lists for each external service:
- Service name and vendor
- Primary role (e.g., model hosting, model weights storage, telemetry/observability, error reporting, customer support, analytics, billing)
- Data types accessed (e.g., prompts/user content, PII, telemetry, logs, metrics)
- Encryption in transit / at rest (Y/N + KMS info if relevant)
- Geographic region(s) where data is processed or stored
- Any known downstream subprocessors (if vendor uses others)
- Pointer to supporting evidence (SOC 2, DPA, SCCs, contract clause, or Drive link)

We have a target of COB Nov 18 to ingest this into our SIG spreadsheet (HubSpot ticket 98765). If there's anything you can't share directly, flag it and we can work through an NDA/channelled evidence upload. Also happy to take a 30-min call this week to walk the list.

We're primarily concerned about telemetry/observability pipelines and where prompt content might be persisted; if you can call that out explicitly that's very helpful.

Thanks,
Claire Owens
Senior Information Security Analyst
Nimbus Health
security@nimbushealth.com

Connor — draft inventory below (still a few items pending confirmation). I attached a CSV (service-delegation-draft.csv) with the columns Claire asked for. High level:

1) Amazon Web Services (AWS) — EC2/EKS, S3
   - Role: model hosting, artifacts, long-term storage (model weights/backups), object store for telemetry archives
   - Data types: model artifacts, anonymized telemetry archives, some support logs (no raw prompts persisted in S3 for hosted API by default)
   - Encryption: TLS in transit; S3 + EBS encryption at rest via AWS KMS (customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/private; Redwood-managed KMS for hosted)
   - Regions: us-west-2 primary for hosted; eu-central-1 for EU customers (multi-region by account)
   - Subprocessors: AWS uses managed partners; full list available in our vendor DPA (see attached pointers)

2) Datadog
   - Role: metrics and alerting, aggregated observability dashboards
   - Data types: aggregated telemetry (latency, error rates, system metrics). We explicitly strip raw prompt content before it goes to Datadog; only anonymized counts and latencies are sent.
   - Encryption: TLS in transit, Datadog-managed encryption at rest; no KMS keys held by Redwood for Datadog (pending legal confirmation if needed)

3) Sentry
   - Role: error reporting (application exceptions)
   - Data types: tracebacks, sanitized error contexts; we scrub user content per telemetry policy

4) Zendesk
   - Role: customer support ticketing (contains customer-provided logs, support attachments)
   - Data types: user-submitted logs and attachments when customers include them in tickets
   - Note: Zendesk subprocessors depend on account region — legal to confirm; mark as 'needs contract check'

5) Vector DB / embeddings store (Pinecone)
   - Role: embeddings index for similarity search (used selectively for product features)
   - Data types: embeddings derived from inputs; we try to avoid storing raw text. Confirm whether any hosted customers enable raw-text indexing (pending)

6) PagerDuty / OpsGenie
   - Role: on-call alerting only (no user data retention)

7) Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive) & Okta
   - Role: corporate communications and identity management
   - Data types: corporate PII (employee data), legal artifacts (Drive)

8) Snowflake (analytics)
   - Role: aggregated billing and product analytics
   - Data types: aggregated usage metrics, billing records (no raw prompts)

Open items I still need: list of Zendesk subprocessors (legal), confirmation on Pinecone retention settings for specific customers, and a short note on whether Datadog receives any low-level request identifiers we should redact. I've attached the draft CSV.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Nice start — a few clarifications from the telemetry side:
- We DO NOT send raw prompt text to Datadog or Sentry. Datadog gets only numeric metrics and health signals. Error reports in Sentry are sanitized; exception payloads go through our scrubber which strips strings that match prompt patterns.
- For long-term retention, aggregated telemetry metrics are exported nightly to an S3 bucket (encrypted) for 2 years; that bucket uses Redwood-managed KMS for hosted customers and customer-managed KMS for Dedicated deployments.
- Telemetry_roster.pdf attached — includes retention windows and links to our telemetry policy page.

Also: Zendesk sometimes stores uploaded files in the vendor's storage layer — legal needs to confirm the storage location for EU accounts. Mark Zendesk rows as 'pending: legal review'.

I'll ping Legal for the Zendesk subprocessors and will update the Drive folder with the telemetry evidence links.

-Marissa
Head of Security Programs | Redwood Inference

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for the patience. Attached is our consolidated inventory (redwood_service_delegation_inventory.csv) and a short text file with links to supporting evidence and Drive artifacts (supporting_evidence_links.txt). Summary of the important points:

- AWS (EC2/EKS, S3): model hosting & storage. Encryption at rest via KMS; hosted vs dedicated KMS noted in CSV. Regions: us-west-2 primary; eu-central-1 for EU customers.
- Datadog / Sentry: metrics & error reporting only. We do not send raw prompts; payloads are sanitized before being forwarded. Daily metrics export retained in encrypted S3 for 2 years.
- Zendesk: customer support ticketing. May contain customer-provided logs/attachments. Zendesk subprocessors are pending legal confirmation (we've flagged this in the CSV).
- Pinecone (vector DB): embeddings store; we avoid raw-text indexing by default — flagged pending for hosted customers who enable advanced features.
- PagerDuty, Snowflake, Google Workspace, Okta: roles and scopes included in CSV.

Next steps:
1) We'll upload SOC 2 / DPA evidence to the Drive link in supporting_evidence_links.txt by EOD Mon Nov 16 (Laura coordinating).
2) Connor / Marissa available for a 30-min walkthrough if you'd like — available Nov 17 or 18 (please propose times).
3) We'll follow up with Legal on Zendesk subprocessors and update the CSV row to 'confirmed' or 'with contract caveat' as appropriate.

If anything in the CSV needs more granularity (e.g., exact KMS key ids for a Dedicated account), tell us the level of detail you need and we can provide it under a secured evidence-sharing channel.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
